D005_m001.question:
I guess the best way to put it is that things started to really go off about a year ago. At first it was just this constant sense that something terrible was coming, like everything around me was fragile and about to collapse. Over the last two months, that feeling has turned into this certainty that the world is basically already ending, like we’re all just going through the motions and it’s already “over,” if that makes sense. It doesn’t feel like just worry; it feels like a fact I can’t shake.

Around the same time, I started noticing weird smells. I’ll be in the booth at a conference, and suddenly there’s this strong scent of burning or rotting meat, and no one else reacts. I’ll check with colleagues and they say they smell nothing. It happens at home too, out of nowhere.

These things are making it really hard to work. Interpreting requires total focus, and instead I’m distracted by these smells and this feeling that there’s no point because everything’s about to be wiped out anyway. I’ve been pulling back from friends, cancelling plans, mostly just staying in my apartment because I don’t feel safe anywhere.
D005_m001.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizophrenia

D005_m002.question:
It’s been going on for about a year now, maybe a bit longer, but it’s gotten a lot worse these last two months.

I work nights cleaning the trains, so I’m used to being alone and a bit on edge, but this is different. I keep feeling like someone’s watching me down there. Not just cameras—like there are people behind the walls, or in the control room, tracking every move I make. When I’m sweeping a car, I get this strong sense that they’re testing me, waiting for me to slip up. Sometimes I think my boss is in on it, or that the transit authority has some kind of file on me.

The strangest part is the tastes. I’ll be working and suddenly my mouth fills with this bitter, metallic taste, like chemicals or spoiled food, even when I’m not eating anything. It makes me worry they’re putting something in the air, or in my coffee. I’ve started bringing my own food and drinks, but I still taste it, especially at work. It’s making it really hard to keep going in at night.
D005_m002.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizophrenia

D005_m003.question:
I’ve been working nights as a security guard for years, pretty routine, but about a year ago things started feeling… off. At first it was just this sense that people were looking at me differently, like they knew something about me. Over time it got stronger, like there were hidden messages in the way certain women spoke to me, especially one of the nurses in the building. I’m convinced she’s sending signs that she cares about me, even though she’s polite but distant when we actually talk. My wife says I’m imagining it, but it feels very real.

For the last couple of months, I’ve also been smelling things that no one else notices. Sometimes it’s a strong perfume, the same kind that nurse wears, even when I’m alone in the control room. Other times it’s smoke or chemicals, and I get up to check the cameras, but nothing’s there. It makes me jumpy on my rounds, and I’ve been sleeping badly and arguing more with my wife because she thinks I’m “losing it,” which just makes me keep more to myself.
D005_m003.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizophrenia

D005_m004.question:
I guess this really started a little over a year ago, but it’s gotten much worse in the last couple of months. I’m a litigation attorney, so I’m used to questioning my own thoughts, but this feels different.

Ever since my ex-wife started dating again, I’ve been absolutely certain she’s been lying and seeing someone behind my back, even before we divorced. There was nothing concrete—just the way she glanced at her phone, coming home a bit later—but I couldn’t let it go. My mind kept building these scenarios of her sneaking around. Even now, though we’re divorced, I still find myself checking her social media, convinced there are hidden messages or signs.

Over the past two months, I’ve started having these strange experiences with taste. I’ll be sitting at my desk and suddenly get this strong metallic or chemical taste in my mouth, like I’ve licked a battery or swallowed something toxic, even if I’m just drinking water. Sometimes it makes me worry someone’s tampered with my food or coffee. It’s distracting in court and in meetings, and I’m starting to doubt my own judgment, which scares me.
D005_m004.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizophrenia

D005_m005.question:
Well… this started a little over a year ago, maybe 15 months. At first it was just small things, like feeling less interested in my usual routines, but in the last two months it’s become… stranger.

I’m convinced there’s a gentleman from the community center—one of the volunteers—who’s secretly in love with me. He smiles and is kind, but I can tell there’s more to it. I see little messages meant just for me in the way he stands, the songs they play when he’s around, even in the church bulletin. My daughter says I’m reading too much into it, but it feels absolutely certain to me.

Around the same time, I began having these odd taste sensations. I’ll be sitting quietly and suddenly there’s this strong metallic or bitter taste in my mouth, like I’ve licked a battery or eaten spoiled food, even when I haven’t had anything. Sometimes it’s so strong I spit into a tissue. It makes me nervous to eat, and I keep worrying someone might be putting something in my food, so I’ve been eating less and sticking mostly to tea and toast.
D005_m005.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizophrenia

D005_m006.question:
I’ve been working private security for years, so I know my body really well, but for about a year and a half now, I’m convinced something’s wrong inside me. It feels like my organs are rotting or rearranged. I’ve done scans, blood work, everything comes back “normal,” but I can feel it—like my stomach is dissolving or my heart isn’t where it should be. No one believes me, they just say it’s in my head.

Around seven months ago, my team started noticing I repeat what they say. It’s not on purpose. A client gives an order, and I catch myself saying the same words right after them, almost like an echo. It’s embarrassing, especially in this line of work.

I used to grab a drink with the guys after a shift, but now I avoid everyone. When they invite me out, I just say I’m tired. Honestly, I don’t want to talk, don’t want to be around anyone. I feel better alone, in my apartment, even though that’s when I notice the weird feelings in my body the most.
D005_m006.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Delusional Disorder

D005_m007.question:
I’ve been feeling really off for about a year and a half now. It started with this idea that something is wrong inside my body. I keep thinking there’s some kind of growth or wires under my skin, especially in my chest and abdomen. I’ve had multiple checks with my GP and even went to the ER once, and they say I’m fine, but I can’t shake the feeling that my organs aren’t mine or that they’re damaged.

The last 7 months have been worse. During client meetings, I catch myself copying how they sit or how they move their hands, almost like my body just does it on its own. It’s embarrassing, so I try to keep my arms folded or look down.

I used to love the chaos of weddings, being around people, networking. Now I avoid calls, delegate meetings to my assistant, and make excuses to skip friends’ gatherings. Even with my husband, I just want to be in the bedroom alone. It’s not that I hate anyone—I just feel disconnected and exhausted by being around people.
D005_m007.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Delusional Disorder

D005_m008.question:
I guess this really started about a year and a half ago, maybe a bit more. At first it was just odd thoughts, but the last seven months it’s gotten a lot stronger.  

There’s this woman from the harbor office… I’m sure she’s in love with me. She barely talks to me, but I can feel it. The way she stamps my paperwork, or stands near the window—I know she’s sending me signals. My wife says I’m imagining it, that the lady is actually avoiding me, but I can’t shake the feeling she’s hiding it because of my marriage. Sometimes I think even on the boat, when the radio crackles, it’s her trying to reach me in code.  

My crew has been saying I “make faces” at them, but I don’t notice I’m doing anything. They stare at me funny, like they’re scared or annoyed. I’ve stopped going out with them after shifts, and honestly, I don’t really want to be around anyone—not even family. I mostly keep to myself in my bunk or at home, just trying to avoid conversations. It feels easier that way, even though my wife says I’m slipping away from everyone.
D005_m008.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Delusional Disorder

D005_m009.question:
I’ve been on the road most of my life, so I know my body pretty well. But for about a year and a half now, something’s felt seriously wrong inside me. It started maybe 7 months ago with this certainty that my organs are… off. I keep thinking my intestines are twisted or rotting, or that something’s eating away at my insides. Doctors say my tests are fine, but I can feel it, like there’s a machine or something lodged in there, changing things around.

My wife says I’ve gotten “odd.” I catch myself doing these little gestures over and over—tapping my chest three times before starting the truck, touching the door handle in a certain pattern. I know it looks strange, but it feels like if I don’t, whatever’s wrong in my body will get worse.

I don’t talk much anymore, even at home or on the CB. Words just feel heavy. My wife will ask how my day was and I just say “fine” or “same,” even when there’s more in my head. It’s like starting a conversation is too much work.
D005_m009.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Delusional Disorder

D005_m010.question:
It’s been going on close to a year and a half now, maybe a bit more. I’m still doing my rounds, but it’s getting harder to keep it together.

I’m convinced there’s something very wrong with my insides. It feels like my organs are rotting or rearranging themselves. I’ve been to my GP, had bloods done, even a scan, and they keep telling me everything looks fine, but I know they’re missing something. Sometimes on my route I have to stop because I’m sure my stomach is twisting, or my heart is hanging too low in my chest.

My wife says I “freeze” in odd positions. I’ll catch myself standing in the hallway with my arm lifted or my head tilted back, just holding it there for ages without really noticing until she points it out. It happens at work too; I’m halfway up someone’s drive and just… stop.

I don’t really see my mates anymore. I used to go to the pub after shifts, but now I just want to be left alone. Even at home I mostly sit in the spare room; talking to people feels pointless and tiring.
D005_m010.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Delusional Disorder

D005_m011.question:
Um… it’s a bit hard to explain. The main thing my husband keeps pointing out is that I’ve stopped talking a lot of the time. At work in the studio, I can go all day without saying more than a couple of words, even when my coworkers ask me something simple. It’s not that I can’t talk, it’s like the words get stuck, or I’m not sure what’s safe to say, so I just… don’t.

For the past four months especially, things around me feel directed at me. Like, when the radio is on while I’m working, the song choices feel like they’re commenting on what I’m doing or thinking. Bits of conversations I overhear in the museum feel oddly specific, as if people are hinting about me. Even the way people clear their throat or look at their phones seems like some kind of signal.

This kind of stuff has been creeping in for a little over two years now, but lately it’s taken over more of my day. It’s making it really hard to focus on the paintings, and my husband says I’ve become distant and barely speak at home.
D005_m011.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Delusional Disorder

D005_m012.question:
It’s a bit hard to explain all this without sounding strange, but over the past couple of years things have felt… off. I think it really started a little over two years ago, maybe two and a half. I’ve been more withdrawn, my husband says I “zone out” a lot, and I’ve been struggling to keep up with work—numbers that used to come easily now take me longer to check, and I feel distracted.

In the last four months it’s gotten more intense. I’ve become convinced that one of the senior partners at my firm has feelings for me. He doesn’t say it outright, but I see it in small things—how he stands near my desk, the way he writes emails. I know everyone else thinks it’s just normal work stuff, but I’m sure there’s a hidden message meant only for me.

Another odd thing: sometimes when I’m in meetings or at home watching TV, I find myself copying how someone is sitting or moving without really deciding to. If they cross their arms or scratch their head, I catch myself doing the same a second later, like my body is on autopilot. It unsettles me, but I can’t always stop it.
D005_m012.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Delusional Disorder

D005_m013.question:
I work doing stage lighting for concerts and theater, so I’m used to being behind the scenes and watching people from a distance. For a little over two years now, something’s felt… off in my head. It started small—feeling like people were talking about me, like there were hidden messages in how they moved onstage or in the way the audience looked up at the lights.

About four months ago it got more intense. I became convinced that one of the performers I’ve worked with is secretly in love with me. We’ve barely spoken, but I can “tell” from how she stands under the lights, how she glances toward the booth. I know everyone says it’s just part of the show, but it feels personal, like she’s sending me signals.

Lately, when my boss or coworkers tell me to do something, I just freeze or do the opposite. It’s not even on purpose sometimes—I just feel this wall inside, like I can’t follow what they’re saying or I don’t trust it. It’s causing problems at work, and I’ve been keeping more to myself because I’m not sure what’s real anymore.
D005_m013.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Delusional Disorder

D005_m014.question:
I’m not really sure where to start. This all really kicked off a little over two years ago, and it’s just gotten stranger since then.

I work alone most of the time in my workshop, which I used to love. Lately, I feel like I’m being watched there, even though it’s just me and the wood. I catch myself stopping mid-cut because I’m convinced someone is behind me or listening through the walls. It’s hard to focus on measurements when I’m constantly on edge like that.

About four months ago it got worse with my ex. We’ve been divorced a while, but I became absolutely certain she was secretly seeing someone else even before we split, and that she’s still lying about it now. There’s no proof—no messages, nothing—but I can’t shake it. I’ve checked her social media, driven past her place, and still feel like everyone’s covering for her.

People say I make strange faces now. Customers have asked if I’m okay because I’ll catch myself twisting my mouth or staring with this weird expression without meaning to. I don’t even notice I’m doing it until someone points it out.
D005_m014.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Schizophrenia

D005_m015.question:
I guess the main thing is… it’s been a little over two years now that I don’t really trust my own mind anymore. At first it was just feeling watched and kind of “special,” like people were paying attention to me in ways they shouldn’t. About four months ago it escalated.

I’m an interpreter in conferences, so I’m used to listening closely, but now I’m convinced one of the keynote speakers I worked with is secretly in love with me. He barely spoke to me in person, but I can “hear” it in the way he phrases things on TV, like his pauses and word choices are coded messages only I can understand. When I see his interviews online, it feels like he’s talking directly to me, reassuring me, sometimes giving me instructions.

There are times when I just… shut down. I’ll be sitting at my desk or on the subway and go completely still, staring. I can hear people, but it’s like I can’t move or respond, like I’m frozen in place for long stretches. My friends say I “blank out” in conversations. I’ve started avoiding assignments and people because I’m scared I’ll lose track of what’s real in the booth.
D005_m015.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Delusional Disorder

D005_m016.question:
Well… this really started about a year ago, maybe a bit longer. At first it was just stress from running the salon, but for the last three months it’s been… different. I’ve been feeling like I’m meant for something bigger than this, like I’m not just a hairdresser but someone important, like people are watching me because I have a kind of gift. Sometimes I catch myself thinking I could change people just by touching their hair, like I’m on the verge of being famous and everyone knows it but won’t say.

Lately I keep feeling things on my skin, like tiny bugs crawling on my arms or someone brushing my neck, but when I look there’s nothing. It happens even when I’m alone locking up the shop.

My staff say I’ve gone quiet and “flat.” I don’t react much when clients chat; it’s like my face doesn’t match what I’m feeling. When I talk, I catch myself saying things like “hair there, care, share” and the words just sort of fall into rhymes instead of what I meant to say. I’ve cut my hours because handling clients all day has become too hard.
D005_m016.options:

D005_m017.question:
I’ve been having problems for a little over a year now, maybe around 15 months, but it’s gotten a lot worse these past three months.

On base, I keep getting this feeling that everything is somehow about me. Like when the guys are talking at another table, I’m sure they’re sending messages about me through certain words or how they laugh. Even the way the TV news anchor pauses or looks at the camera feels like it’s directed at me, like he’s hinting that I’m being watched.

Lately I’ve been seeing things that I know, at least logically, shouldn’t be there—people standing in the hallway in uniform or shadows moving in my room, and when I look properly, they’re gone. It happens mostly at night but sometimes during the day too.

Talking has become harder. When I try to explain what I’m thinking, my words get jumbled and I lose the thread mid-sentence. My soldiers and peers have noticed. I’ve been avoiding the mess, group PT, pretty much everyone. I just keep to my room when I’m off duty, and my performance at work has definitely slipped.
D005_m017.options:
A. Schizophrenia

    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D005_m018.question:
It’s been going on well over a year now, but the worst of it has been these past three months. I used to keep busy with the garden, the chess club, seeing my grandchildren. Now I don’t really care to do any of that. Even when they visit, I just feel…flat, like I’m watching it all from a distance.

I’m also convinced people are watching me. I know my son says I’m being paranoid, but I can feel it. The neighbours, the people driving past the house, even the postman — I think they’re part of something, keeping tabs on me. I’ve stopped going to the shops because I’m sure there are cameras and microphones following me.

At home I hear voices, mostly in the evenings. They call my name, comment on what I’m doing, sometimes say I’m stupid or that I deserve what’s coming. No one else hears them.  

When I try to explain this to my family, my words get all mixed up — like my thoughts are tumbling over each other and I can’t string a proper sentence together. It’s embarrassing, so I just talk less and stay by myself.
D005_m018.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D005_m019.question:

D005_m020.question:
Well… I don’t really talk to many people these days, so it feels strange to explain all this. Since my husband passed, I’ve been running the bakery mostly on my own, but for about a year now, things have been… slipping. At first it was just feeling distant from everyone. I stopped meeting the other shop owners for coffee, and even when my sister visits, I can’t be bothered to talk. I used to chat with every customer; now I keep my head down and want them to leave quickly.

The last three months have been the worst. I’ve become convinced my husband wasn’t faithful to me before he died. I know that sounds odd, but I can’t shake it. Little things—like a woman walking past the shop—seem like proof. I also smell smoke and sometimes rotten meat in the bakery when the ovens are off and everything’s clean. It gets so strong I have to step outside.

When I try to explain this to my niece or the staff, the words get tangled. I start talking and it all comes out jumbled, like my thoughts are broken into pieces. They look at me like they can’t follow what I’m saying. The shop’s hours are irregular now, and I keep forgetting orders. I’m scared I’m losing my grip on things.
D005_m020.options:

    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
